correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=2 the root-chord arc split has exactly M_k M_(n-1-k) valid matchings and independent uniform within-arc diagrams. Their crossing means add and subtract from n(n-1)/6 to give negative conditional shift -[(n-1)+k(n-1-k)]/3. Rooting at one uniform chord yields the exact covariance. K=0,n-1 are the simple chords; the k=1,n-2 layer yields -2n/[3(2n-1)]. All further layers are O(1/n) in covariance by the ratio a_(k+1)/a_k=(2k+1)/(2n-3-2k) and geometric-plus-central-tail bounds. The script verify.py separately enumerates all 146598 matchings through n=7, verifies 27 conditional splits, and checks 499 further exact identities up to n=500. Finite checks are not infinite proofs.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The classical component generating function marks the number of components without recording crossings, and the Touchard--Riordan crossing polynomial records crossings without recording isolated components. These marginals do not logically determine mixed covariance. Combining them into a marked joint theory requires additional component-size/crossing decomposition; no inspected published theorem presents the displayed all-n kernel or its nonzero rare-event correction.

evidence: The classical simple-chord covariance is -2n(n-1)/[3(2n-1)] in this model, whereas the full isolated-chord covariance has additional terms indexed 1 <= k <= n-2.

The additional covariance converges to -1/3 although the expected number of additional chords is 1/(2n)+O(n^-2); thus the simple-chord formula cannot imply the full claim by replacing isolated by simple without a new moment calculation.

Flajolet--Noy (https://algo.inria.fr/flajolet/Publications/FlNo00.pdf) supplies a crossing mean and component means separately; Acan (https://arxiv.org/html/1501.01489v1) supplies isolation probability asymptotics, not cross moments.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The event of being a simple chord is strictly contained in degree-zero isolation. The difference is not negligible in covariance even asymptotically. General elementary random-graph intuition may suggest a negative sign, but does not produce the exact double-factorial summation or the -1/3 non-simple correction.

originality.rationale: The exact finite mixed moment for every degree-zero chord and every crossing pair, and its asymptotic non-simple correction, are not in the inspected full-text studies. The earlier simple-chord law is strictly narrower: its omitted contribution tends to -1/3. The marginal isolated-chord and crossing distributions and connected-crossing coefficient tables do not by themselves specify this joint covariance. A general but unlocated joint-component/crossing enumerator remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: Older unindexed bivariate component-size versus crossing generating functions, knot-diagram literature, or alternate notation for joint degree-zero / crossing moments may encode the same formula.
The connected-diagram crossing polynomial plus a separate decomposition could be refined into a joint isolated-component marker; such a derivation was not located as a prior result.
No literature search is exhaustive, and the resulting originality assessment has not received independent review.

value.rationale: Isolated vertices and edge count of a random chord intersection graph are canonical joint network observables, and the finite double-factorial expression quantifies their exact negative dependence. The derived -1/3 covariance correction arises from nonsimple isolated chords that occur with vanishing mean 1/(2n)+O(1/n^2), a nontrivial second-order contribution not obtainable by substituting the simple-chord statistic. This separates local adjacency isolation from global zero crossing degree and identifies a finite-size structural boundary.
